key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over weeks to months. LOCATION: VARIABLE depending on tumor location. DURATION: Progressive over weeks to months. CHARACTER: VARIABLE symptoms. AGGRAVATING: ACTIVITY, stress, fatigue. RELIEVING: SUPPORTIVE care, medications. TIMING: Progressive over weeks to months. SEVERITY: 4-8/10, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: VARIABLE - headache, seizures, vision problems, cognitive changes, may have focal neurological deficits. KEY POSITIVES: Variable symptoms, may have MRI changes, may have focal neurological deficits. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no neck stiffness, no photophobia.

red_flags: Severe neurological deficits with altered mental status - possible severe brain tumor, call 911
Signs of increased intracranial pressure - severe headache, vomiting, altered mental status - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of brainstem involvement - dysphagia, dysarthria, ataxia - call 911
Signs of respiratory failure - difficulty breathing, cyanosis, altered mental status - call 911
